definitions.explanation: To a great degree; used to intensify adjectives and verbs.

examples.japanese: この{料理|りょうり}はとてもおいしいです。
とても{疲|つか}れました。
とても{楽|たの}しかったです。
この{映画|えいが}はとても{面白|おもしろ}かったです。また{見|み}たいです。
examples.english: This movie was very interesting. I want to watch it again.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}の{春|はる}はとてもきれいです。{桜|さくら}の{花|はな}が{咲|さ}くと、{多|おお}くの{人|ひと}が{公園|こうえん}に{行|い}きます。
examples.english: Spring in Japan is very beautiful. When the cherry blossoms bloom, many people go to parks.

notes:
とても is a common adverb meaning "very" or "extremely." It's polite and versatile, suitable for most situations.

USAGE:
- Modifies adjectives: とても{大|おお}きい (very big)
- Modifies verbs: とても{疲|つか}れた (very tired)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- すごく: very (more casual, emphatic)
- {大変|たいへん}: very, terribly (can imply difficulty)
- {非常|ひじょう}に: extremely (formal)
- とっても: very (casual variant of とても)

NEGATIVE PATTERN:
とても + negative = "cannot possibly"
- とても{食|た}べられない: I can't possibly eat it
- とても{無理|むり}だ: It's absolutely impossible

REGISTER:
とても is neutral and appropriate for both spoken and written Japanese.
